title: Trial run on a second repo with no legacy tree to import

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
All prior dogfooding was on slicer's own `.slicer/`, which was born from `migrate`. This
validates the greenfield path — a fresh project with no legacy markdown — through init, both
intake routes (outline import and individual add), authoring, the newer query commands, and the
render/check/verify gate.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
In a throwaway git repo: `slicer init`; `import --skeleton` + a title-dependency outline
(dry-run then apply) and `add`; `promote`/`edit`/`note` (bare and promoted); `prose edit
goals`; `next --start`, `deps --format mermaid`, `find`, `status`, `stats`, `sort`, `log`;
`render` (ROADMAP.md + ROADMAP.html), `check`, `verify`, `done`, `remove --dry-run`; commit and
confirm check is green from a clean tree. File any greenfield-specific friction.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Validation only — no src changes. Findings filed into the roadmap.
